mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the monthly FEDFUNDS rate above 4% for two consecutive months reduces the real discount rate applied to future equity valuations, thereby pushing S&P 500 20-day forward returns into negative territory.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4% and remains above for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in at least 70% of similar high-inflation regimes, or FEDFUNDS decline after trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 4% for three consecutive months, labor market slack increases, reducing corporate profit expectations and driving negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in less than 30% of historical expanding-labor-market regimes, or UNRATE recovers above 4% within 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly increases in HOUST and GDPC1 exceeding 5% and 8% respectively for two months indicate accelerating business and consumer demand, which elevates S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST up >5% and GDPC1 up >8% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: No significant correlation between the combined demand signal and 20-day forward returns in 10 historical early-cycle expansions (Pearson IC > 0.2).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in INDPRO above 105 (monthly) followed by a decline suggests supply-side constraints easing, which amplifies S&P 500 5-day forward returns during a supply-chain recovery phase.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 105 for one month then < 105 in the following month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns fail to outperform baseline by at least 0.5% in 15 post-shock episodes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains below 3% for four consecutive months, the central bank's policy rate is interpreted as restrictive, depressing equity valuations and producing negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are non-negative in 80% of historical rate-normalization episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in PAYEMS exceeding 160,000 for a month followed by a drop suggests labor market stress, lowering corporate optimism and driving negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 160,000 for one month then < 160,000 next month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly worse than baseline in 50 labor-market-tightness regimes (IC < -0.1).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous strength in both HOUST (>120) and RSAFS (>700M) for two consecutive months signals robust demand across consumer and investment sectors, forecasting positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 120 and RSAFS > 700M for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns miss the 95% prediction interval in 40 historical dual-sector demand expansions (Monte-Carlo).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in UNRATE below 3% for six months indicates soft labor costs, lowering inflationary pressures and supporting S&P 500 60-day forward returns in deflationary regimes.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns underperform by more than 1% in 40 historical deflationary regimes (out-of-sample).
